title: DILI on HRZE and friends
dek: INH, RIF, and PZA share the liver. Stop the right drug, not the alphabet by panic. Reintroduction order is a protocol, not folklore.
story: First-line TB therapy is a hepatotoxicity machine: isoniazid (especially slow NAT2 acetylators, alcohol, pregnancy, HIV), pyrazinamide (dose and duration), and rifampin (cholestatic and mixed pictures). Ethambutol is the usual liver-spare companion. Combined DILI is why programmes check ALT/AST/bilirubin at baseline and when the patient turns yellow, nauseated, or just “off.”

Thresholds vary; a common teaching cut is ALT >3× ULN with symptoms or >5× without, or bilirubin rise — use the local SOP. Stop H, R, and Z together when the liver is in trouble. Do not keep PZA “because it’s only month two.” Bridge with liver-spare drugs (EMB, an FQ, sometimes AMK/LZD in ugly cases) so you never monotherapy a cavity.
Reintroduction is staged (often R then H then Z last or never) once enzymes fall. PZA is the usual permanent casualty. Pretomanid and BDQ also have hepatic labels; BPaLM is not DILI-proof.
deepTitle: Hy’s law and the other yellow
deep: Gilbert’s and rifampin unconjugated bilirubin can scare people. Fractionate.
Viral hepatitis unmasking on HRZE is a differential, not a rarity in some regions.
3HP and HPMZ still contain INH and a rifamycin; 1HP is not a liver holiday.
Do not rechallenge PZA after severe DILI to “complete intensive phase.”

visual.caption: DILI: recognise, stop H/R/Z, bridge without monotherapy, reintroduce with Z last or never.

example.title: ALT 420, still on HRZE month 1
example.setup: Symptoms plus ALT 8× ULN, bilirubin 2.4, smear still 2+.

steps.title: Stop H, R, Z today
steps.body: Keep EMB if optic screen allows; add an FQ so two agents cover the cavity.

steps.title: Reintroduce later with a protocol
steps.body: R then H; leave Z out after this severity.

example.takeaway: DILI management is stop-together, bridge-plural, reintroduce-staged.

check.prompt: When HRZE DILI is diagnosed, the usual stop set is:
check.why: EMB is usually kept as a companion in the bridge, not the primary liver offender.

whyWrong.Moxifloxacin only: May be the bridge, not the stop.

check.prompt: Bridging with EMB alone during DILI in cavitary TB is wrong because:
choices: Monotherapy selects EmbB mutants while bacilli still replicate
check.answer: Monotherapy selects EmbB mutants while bacilli still replicate
check.why: Always ≥2 likely-active drugs in the bridge.

check.prompt: On the flow map, reintroduction hangs off:
choices: The liver-spare bridge after stopping H/R/Z
check.answer: The liver-spare bridge after stopping H/R/Z
check.why: You do not reintroduce from a still-hot liver.
